Shared list-endpoint helpers (``ig.platform.api``).

Dynamic filters, multi-sort, and pagination for the JSON list
endpoints, driven entirely by per-endpoint **allowlists**: an explicit
``{query field name → mapped column}`` dict. Nothing is ever reflected
off a model from request input — a field outside the allowlist is a
400, never an attribute lookup.

Request grammar:

- Filters: ``field=value`` (equality) or ``field[op]=value`` with ops
  eq, ne, lt, lte, gt, gte, like, in (comma-separated), isnull
  (true/false). Values are coerced to the column's Python type;
  datetimes must be aware ISO-8601 (the clock law's database boundary
  rejects naive values).
- Sort: ``sort=field:dir,field:dir`` with dir asc (default) or desc.
- Pagination: ``page`` (1-based) and ``per_page``, capped at
  ``MAX_PER_PAGE``.

Every violation raises :class:`QueryValidationError`, which the API
package maps to a 400 response.

Team dashboards (``ig.platform.api``): read-only aggregates.

Three views over the same world: queue health per team (how much READY
work each team faces), auditor performance over a caller-chosen window
(claims and closes per auditor), and a trailing-30-day production
rollup (closed reviews and recovered opportunity per team per day).

The production rollup is the spec's second and final declared raw-SQL
spot — its timestamp comparison renders values the way ``UTCDateTime``
stores them, exactly like the stale sweep's. The other two dashboards
stay ORM.

value:
text('
    SELECT users.team AS team,
           DATE(invoice_history.at) AS day,
           COUNT(*) AS closed_count,
           SUM(COALESCE(invoices.opportunity, 0)) AS recovered_opportunity
    FROM invoice_history
    JOIN users ON users.short_name = invoice_history.actor
    JOIN invoices ON invoices.id = invoice_history.invoice_id
    WHERE invoice_history.to_status IN (:closed, :no_review)
      AND invoice_history.at >= :window_start
    GROUP BY users.team, DATE(invoice_history.at)
    ORDER BY users.team, day
    ')

docstring:
The scheduled-task tick executor (spec §7).

The component ``ig.platform.scheduler``. All delayed behavior in
InvoiceGuard — hold rechecks now; compliance fallbacks, creep-back
scans, nightly recalcs, and stale sweeps in later phases — is a row in
``scheduled_tasks``, executed by :func:`tick` when due. There are no
sleeps, no timers, and no threads: whoever owns the clock (the CLI's
real clock or the simulation driver's controlled one) decides when a
tick happens.
What one executor pass did.
A due task names no registered handler — always a bug, never skipped.
Map every known task_name to its handler (spec §7).

Run every due task exactly once, in ``(due_at, id)`` order.

Due means ``due_at <= clock.now()`` and ``completed_at`` NULL. The
id tiebreaker keeps ordering deterministic when a controlled clock
hands several tasks the same instant. The due set is snapshotted
before execution starts, so tasks a handler schedules — a hold
re-check re-arming itself — wait for a later tick.

Each task is its own transaction. A handler that raises has its
partial work rolled back and the task is still marked completed,
with an ERROR log carrying the failure — consumed loudly, never
silently, and never retried (the table has no retry columns; an
uncompleted failure would re-fail on every subsequent tick). An
unknown ``task_name`` raises :class:`UnknownTaskError` instead:
that is a wiring bug, and the task stays uncompleted so a fixed
registry can resume exactly where the tick stopped.
signature: (session: Session, clock: Clock, registry: dict[str, TaskHandler] | None=None) -> TickSummary

docstring:
The pipeline stages (``ig.spine.*``).

Stages hand off by direct function dispatch — intake routes a file to
the invoice parser, the parser invokes line mapping, and so on down the
chain. Delayed work never sleeps or spawns threads: it is written to the
``scheduled_tasks`` table and executed by the platform scheduler's tick.

Benchmark scoring: the HTTP client stage in front of roll-up.

The component ``ig.spine.benchmark-scoring`` (spec Act 2, §8). Every
findings branch converges here: the stage builds the invoice's peer
features, asks the benchmark service to score them, stores the two
deltas on the invoice, and dispatches roll-up. The service being down
never stops scoring — after ``BENCHMARK_RETRY_LIMIT`` immediate
attempts the stage logs the fallback and proceeds with both deltas
None, exactly as the spec's outage window expects.

This is the only place benchmark HTTP is ever called; recomputation
paths read the stored delta columns. Transport is stdlib
``urllib.request`` behind the single seam ``_request_score`` so tests
never need a live server.
Item codes under a contract active when the invoice arrived.

The peer-comparison features the benchmark service scores.

``line_class_mix`` is each class's share of extended price.
``alt_source_pct`` is the share of material spend on items with no
contract active at ``received_at`` — buying outside contract is
alternate sourcing. Evaluating contract activity at the invoice's
own timestamp (never the current clock) keeps the features, and so
the score, replay-stable.

One POST to the benchmark service; the tests' transport seam.

The body is serialized with sorted keys so identical features are
identical bytes on the wire. Raises on transport failure, a
non-JSON body, or a response missing either delta.

Score one invoice against its peers, then dispatch roll-up.

Bounded immediate retries (no sleeps — the clock law owns time);
the retry count is fixed so an outage window produces the same
number of fallback log lines on every run. Success stores both
deltas; exhaustion leaves them None. Either way roll-up runs —
scoring always completes.

docstring:
Compliance-report intake: external findings join InvoiceGuard's own.

The component ``ig.spine.compliance-intake`` (spec Act 2). The external
contract-compliance system issues one report per invoice revision as a
``*_compliance.json`` file; intake stores the structured report,
denormalizes the total score onto the invoice, and converts each rule
item into a COMPLIANCE finding so external findings sit alongside the
rules engine's.

A report's arrival can also be what completes scoring (spec Act 2's
compliance wait): an invoice deferred behind an armed
``skip_compliance`` task finalizes now, and one already finalized gets
an in-place re-roll-up so a late report still moves its weight. The
status checks keep finalization exactly-once — see
``invoiceguard.spine.rollup``.

Returns the new report, or ``None`` for a redelivery (the invoice
already has one — logged, treated as success). Raises on contract
violations — intake routes the file to ``error/``. After storing:
an invoice already finalized (READY / CLAIMED / IN_REVIEW)
recomputes in place; one still RECEIVED behind an armed
``skip_compliance`` task finalizes now; one still RECEIVED

find; terminal invoices keep the report with no recompute — they
are never re-scored.

Price creep-back detection: the slow-path revision-chain scan.

The component ``ig.spine.creepback`` (spec Act 2, §7). Prior-audit
compliance arms a ``creepback_scan`` task for every revision that has a
reviewed prior; the handler here walks the full revision chain looking
for the pattern: a line the supplier reduced after an auditor's
correction, accepted at the lower rate, then quietly raised again on a
later revision. Each occurrence records the clawed-back dollars as a
CREEPBACK finding, plus one invoice-level summary finding.

Detection runs against the scan target's *current* rates: a transient
raise that was reversed again before this revision does not trip. When
one line carries several adoption events across the chain, the latest
one wins — ``persist_finding`` dedupes on (invoice, line, rule), so the
rule must resolve to exactly one deterministic finding per line.

Map line_number to the rate last accepted after a correction.

An adoption event on a line: the auditor's review of revision Rᵢ
requested a rate below Rᵢ's, and Rᵢ₊₁ carries exactly that rate.
Walking oldest-to-newest overwrites earlier events, so the latest
adoption per line wins.
Index an invoice's lines by line_number for chain comparison.

Fold fresh creep-back findings into an already-scored invoice.

The scan usually runs after the invoice went READY, and CREEPBACK's
only scoring effect is the roll-up weight multiplier — without this
recompute it would wait for the nightly recalculation. Roll-up
no-ops for invoices not yet finalized or already terminal.

docstring:
Scheduled-task handler for ``creepback_scan`` (spec §7).

``args`` carries ``invoice_id``, the newest revision to judge. Walks
the chain oldest-to-newest collecting accepted rates (auditor
requested a lower rate, next revision adopted it exactly), then
compares this revision's rates against them. Chains shorter than the
pattern are a logged no-op. Re-scans are idempotent through
``persist_finding``. Ends by asking roll-up to fold the new findings
into an already-scored invoice's weight.
signature: (session: Session, clock: Clock, args: dict) -> None

docstring:
Feedback capture and carry-forward across revisions (spec Act 4).

The component ``ig.spine.feedback``. An auditor's judgement on a finding
— valid exception, rule misfire, notes — is one ``finding_feedback``
row. Feedback never mutates or deletes the finding itself: roll-up reads
it through ``Finding.effective_amount()`` on the *next* recalculation
(the nightly recalc is the vehicle), never at capture time.

Replacement is delete-then-insert: ``finding_id`` is unique, so a second
auditor's feedback removes the first row and inserts its own.

Carry-forward keeps a judged issue judged: when revision N has a prior,
feedback on the prior's findings is cloned onto N's findings that match
on ``(line_number, rule_name)`` — original auditor preserved, ``cloned``
set. It runs on every pipeline path where a prior revision exists
(feedback is independent of review reports: an auditor can except a
finding with no report ever dropped), and again after the slow-path
creep-back scan for the findings that arrive late. Idempotent: a
finding that already has feedback is never overwritten.

Clone the prior revision's feedback onto matching findings.

A finding on ``invoice`` matches a prior-revision finding with the
same ``(line_number, rule_name)`` (invoice-level NULL matches NULL).
Matching feedback is cloned with the original auditor and flags,
marked ``cloned`` — so the cloned judgement zeroes amounts on N's
recalc exactly like the original did. Findings that already carry
feedback are left alone, which makes re-runs (the pipeline hook,
then the creep-back scan) idempotent. Returns the number of rows
cloned; a no-prior invoice is a zero no-op. Never commits.
signature: (session: Session, clock: Clock, invoice: Invoice) -> int

docstring:
Upsert one auditor's feedback on one finding (spec Act 4, §3).

Honors the unique constraint by delete-then-insert: existing
feedback — anyone's, cloned or not — is removed and the new row
inserted. Deliberately schedules no recalculation: the spec applies
feedback on the next recalc, and the nightly recalc is that
vehicle. Never commits; the caller owns the transaction. Raises
``LookupError`` for an unknown finding.
signature: (session: Session, clock: Clock, auditor: User, finding_id: int, *, valid_exception: bool=False, rule_misfire: bool=False, feedback_text: str | None=None, misfire_text: str | None=None) -> FindingFeedback

docstring:
The intake poller: nothing enters InvoiceGuard except through here.

The component ``ig.spine.intake`` (spec Act 1). One poll is one scan of
the drop directory: each file is routed by a filename-suffix match
against the dispatch table, handled, and relocated by the file
lifecycle. There is no loop and no sleep — the CLI or the simulation
driver decides when a scan happens, per the clock law.
What one drop-directory scan did.
First suffix match in ROUTES wins; None means unrecognized.

Scan the drop directory once and route every file.

Files are taken in sorted filename order — directory-listing order
is nondeterministic, and identical runs must process identically.
Each file is its own transaction: a handler failure rolls back that
file's work, moves the file to ``error/``, and the scan continues.
Handlers never commit.
signature: (session: Session, clock: Clock, areas: FileAreas) -> PollSummary

docstring:
Invoice parse: one dropped XML file becomes one invoice row.

The component ``ig.spine.invoice-parse`` (spec Act 1). Reads an
``*_invoice.xml`` file per the contract in ``docs/file-formats.md``,
resolves the supplier by its unique code, and creates the invoice row
holding the full parsed payload as JSON plus the key columns. The birth
branch happens here: network suppliers start ``RECEIVED`` and continue
into line mapping; non-network suppliers are born ``LAPSED`` and stop.

A redelivered file — an already-existing ``(supplier, invoice_number,
revision)`` — never creates a duplicate: it is logged and treated as
success so intake moves the file to ``processed/``.
Raised when an invoice XML file is malformed or violates the contract.
Raised when the file's supplier_code matches no supplier row.
Optional boolean element: omitted means false (docs/file-formats.md).
Parse one <line>; keys in fixed literal order for byte-stable JSON.

Parse a file, create its invoice row, and dispatch line mapping.

Returns the new invoice, or ``None`` for a redelivery. Raises
``InvoiceParseError`` / ``UnknownSupplierError`` on contract
violations — intake treats any exception as a handler failure and
routes the file to ``error/``. Never commits: intake owns the
per-file transaction.
signature: (session: Session, clock: Clock, path: Path) -> Invoice | None

docstring:
Parse one ``*_invoice.xml`` into the payload dict stored on the row.

Strict against ``docs/file-formats.md``: the root tag, every required
element, and every value type are validated, and any violation
(including unparseable XML) raises ``InvoiceParseError``. Optional
elements land as ``None``. Payload keys are built in a fixed literal
order so ``payload_json`` serializes byte-stably across runs.

Stale sweep: lapse invoices that sat unworked too long.

The component ``ig.spine.lapse-lifecycle`` (spec Act 5). A daily
``stale_sweep`` scheduled task flips still-pending invoices older than
the cutoff to ``LAPSED``. The cutoff is ``lapse_after_days`` (config)
plus ``LAPSE_GRACE_DAYS`` of hardcoded grace, measured back from the
injected clock.

The sweep deliberately protects: any status outside the sweep-lapsable
set (terminals are never touched), rows missing a received timestamp,
and invoices whose denormalized ``invoices.compliance_score`` is at or
above ``COMPLIANCE_SCORE_CRITICAL``. Per the spec amendments, that
column is Act 5's protection signal — intentionally distinct from
roll-up's Σ COMPLIANCE finding amounts, which an auditor's exception
can zero; sweep protection survives such feedback.

The candidate query is the spec's first declared raw-SQL spot. Its
timestamp comparison must render values the way ``UTCDateTime`` stores
them — naive UTC, via ``utc_naive`` — and everything after the id
select stays ORM so every lapse flows through the one transition
helper and writes history.

value:
text('
    SELECT id FROM invoices
    WHERE status IN (:ready, :received)
      AND received_at IS NOT NULL
      AND received_at < :cutoff
      AND (compliance_score IS NULL OR compliance_score < :critical)
    ORDER BY id
    ')

docstring:
Scheduled-task handler for ``stale_sweep`` (spec §7, Act 5).

Selects the sweepable candidates in one raw-SQL pass, then lapses
each through the transition helper (actor ``system.stale-sweep``)
so history rows are written. Emits one summary event and returns
the number of invoices lapsed (the tick executor ignores it; the
CLI wrapper prints it). ``args`` is unused — the sweep always
covers the whole backlog. Never commits; the tick executor (or the
CLI wrapper) owns the transaction.
signature: (session: Session, clock: Clock, args: dict) -> int

docstring:
Line mapping: flatten the payload and settle the revision chain.

The component ``ig.spine.line-mapping`` (spec Act 1). Takes an invoice
row born by the parser, flattens its stored JSON payload into queryable
columns and ``invoice_lines`` rows, writes NOTE findings for supplier
line notes, and links the invoice to its prior revision — lapsing the
prior or inheriting its auditor. A prior that is mid-review defers
completion through a ``hold_recheck`` scheduled task (spec §7).

Supersede-or-inherit logic lives here and nowhere else. Every function
is re-entrant: the hold path re-invokes mapping, so line creation is
guarded and findings go through the idempotent persist seam.
The single exit of mapping: log completion, then hand off to rules.
signature: (session: Session, clock: Clock, invoice: Invoice) -> None

docstring: Write a NOTE finding for every line carrying a supplier note.
signature: (session: Session, clock: Clock, invoice: Invoice) -> None

docstring: Locate the chain predecessor: same supplier and number, revision − 1.
Copy the payload's invoice-level fields onto queryable columns.
Carry the prior's auditor onto the new revision, when it has one.

Create one invoice_lines row per payload line, exactly once.

``invoice_lines`` has no uniqueness on (invoice_id, line_number), so
re-entry after a hold must be guarded here: an invoice that already
has lines is already mapped.
Queue the next recheck; args keys are in fixed order for byte-stable JSON.
signature: (session: Session, clock: Clock, invoice: Invoice, first_hold_at: datetime) -> None

docstring: Supersede a prior that is not mid-review: lapse it, or link only.
signature: (session: Session, clock: Clock, invoice: Invoice, prior: Invoice) -> None

docstring:
Hand a mapped invoice to ``ig.spine.rules-engine`` (spec Act 2).

Called exactly once per mapped invoice, at mapping completion; the
rules engine dispatches onward through the rest of the scoring
chain.
signature: (session: Session, clock: Clock, invoice: Invoice) -> None

docstring:
Map one invoice; return True when mapping completed.

Flattens the payload into columns and lines, writes NOTE findings,
and settles the revision chain. When the prior revision is mid-review
(CLAIMED or IN_REVIEW), a ``hold_recheck`` task is scheduled instead
of settling and False is returned — ``run_hold_recheck`` finishes the
job later. Never flushes past what autoflush does; never commits —
the calling stage owns the transaction.
signature: (session: Session, clock: Clock, invoice: Invoice) -> bool

docstring:
Scheduled-task handler for ``hold_recheck`` (spec §7).

``args`` carries ``invoice_id`` and ``first_hold_at`` (ISO string,
stamped at the first hold and carried unchanged through every
re-schedule so the expiry window cannot be reset). Outcomes:

- the held invoice itself became terminal (a newer revision lapsed
  it while it waited): abandon — mapping never completes for a
  terminal invoice;
- prior still mid-review, within HOLD_EXPIRY_HOURS of the first
  hold: schedule another recheck;
- prior still mid-review at or past expiry: give up waiting —
  inherit the auditor, lapse the prior, complete mapping;
- prior left mid-review: inherit the auditor and settle by the
  prior's current status, then complete mapping.
signature: (session: Session, clock: Clock, args: dict) -> None

docstring:
Prior-audit compliance: review-report intake and the revision check.

The component ``ig.spine.prior-audit-compliance`` (spec Act 2). Two
halves live here because they share one contract:

- The intake handler for ``*_review.json`` files stores an auditor's
  prior review — the corrections the supplier was asked to make — per
  ``docs/file-formats.md``.
- The pipeline stage, dispatched from the rules engine, compares a
  revision against its prior's review: every correction the supplier
  failed to apply becomes a CORRECTION_IGNORED finding, the prior
  revision records whether the supplier accepted the review, and a
  creep-back scan is armed for the slow path.

Correction comparison is exact: a requested rate counts as adopted only
when the new line carries precisely that rate, and a removal only when
the line is gone. A line the supplier removed entirely satisfies a rate
request too — the charge is gone. Removal dominates when a correction
carries both fields.
Raised when a review-report file violates the format contract.
Raised when a review report references no known invoice revision.

Why this correction counts as ignored, or None when applied.

Removal dominates a rate request; a line absent from the revision
satisfies a rate request (the charge is gone).
Validate one corrections[] entry; keys in fixed literal order.
Resolve the reviewed invoice by its business-key triple.
The review report already stored for one revision, if any.
Arm the slow-path scan; due immediately means the next tick.
signature: (session: Session, clock: Clock, invoice: Invoice) -> None

docstring:
Hand the invoice to ``ig.spine.benchmark-scoring`` (spec Act 2).

Called exactly once per invoice that passes through prior-audit,
short-circuit included — benchmark scoring is the convergence point
all findings branches funnel into.
signature: (session: Session, clock: Clock, invoice: Invoice) -> None

docstring:
Store one review report against the invoice revision it reviewed.

Returns the new report, or ``None`` for a redelivery (the reviewed
invoice already has one — logged and treated as success so intake
moves the file to ``processed/``). Raises on contract violations —
intake routes the file to ``error/``. Never commits: intake owns the
per-file transaction.
signature: (session: Session, clock: Clock, path: Path) -> ReviewReport | None

docstring:
Parse one ``*_review.json`` into a validated payload dict.

Strict against ``docs/file-formats.md``: required fields, types, the
disposition enum, and the at-least-one-correction-field rule are all
enforced; any violation (including unparseable JSON) raises
``ReviewReportParseError``. Optional fields land as ``None`` /
``False``.

Compare a revision against its prior's review report (spec Act 2).

Dispatched from the rules engine for every mapped invoice. Without a
prior revision, or without a review report on the prior, the stage
short-circuits straight to benchmark scoring. Otherwise every
correction the supplier ignored becomes a CORRECTION_IGNORED finding
(category CORRECTION, amount 0), the prior records supplier
acceptance (ACCEPTED iff every correction was applied), and a
creep-back scan is armed for the slow path before dispatching
onward.

Whenever a prior revision exists — review report or not, because
feedback arrives through the API independently of reports — the
prior's feedback is carried forward onto this revision's matching
findings before benchmark scoring, so a judged issue is never
re-judged (``ig.spine.feedback``).
signature: (session: Session, clock: Clock, invoice: Invoice) -> None

docstring:
Queue surfacing, GetNext, and the direct claim (spec Act 4).

The component ``ig.spine.queue``. Turns the scored backlog into each
auditor's prioritized queue and claims work through the one transition
helper.

The invoice-to-team ownership rule (implicit in the spec, stated here):
an invoice is eligible for an auditor if and only if it carries at least
one finding whose category is listed under the auditor's team in the
config ``team_to_categories`` mapping. An invoice whose findings all
belong to other teams — or an auditor whose team owns no categories —
surfaces nothing.

Eligibility beyond ownership: status ``READY``, unclaimed, supplier not
on the config exclusion list, and neither the credit-memo nor the
disputed-hold flag set. Ordering is by weight descending with
``PRIOR_AUDITOR_BOOST`` applied — as an ordering-time multiplier only,
never stored — when the auditor touched the invoice's revision chain
within the last ``SAVE_FOR_AUDITOR_BUSINESS_DAYS`` business day, then
by invoice id as the deterministic tiebreak.
A direct claim was refused; the invoice is unchanged.
Reactivation refused: the LAPSED invoice has a newer revision.
The caller's role does not allow a direct claim.
Is there a direct successor? Chains are linked lists, so one hop.
The finding categories the auditor's team owns, as enum members.
Ids of ``invoice`` and every prior revision in its chain.

Did ``auditor`` touch this revision chain since ``cutoff``?

A touch is a history row the auditor wrote (actor = short name), or
a chain member the auditor currently holds via ``claimed_by`` —
inherited claims carry a system actor, so recency for those rides
on the member's latest history row instead.
signature: (session: Session, invoice: Invoice, auditor: User, cutoff: datetime) -> bool

docstring:
Invoices surfaceable to a team owning ``categories``.

The eligibility rules shared by per-auditor queues and the
queue-health dashboard: status READY, unclaimed, supplier not
excluded, neither flag set, and at least one finding in an owned
category.

The eligible-invoice query for one auditor (module docstring rules).

Returns a ``Select`` of :class:`Invoice` rows; ranking happens in
:func:`rank_queue` because the prior-auditor boost needs a
revision-chain walk the query cannot express.
signature: (session: Session, config: InvoiceGuardConfig, auditor: User) -> Select

docstring:
The instant ``days`` business days before ``now``, weekends skipped.

Steps back one calendar day per business day, then keeps stepping
while the landing day is a Saturday or Sunday, preserving the time
of day. Pure and clock-driven: ``now`` comes from the injected
clock at every call site.

Directly claim one invoice, reactivating LAPSED when sanctioned.

Role-gated to audit managers and admins — enforced here as well as
at the API layer, because the simulation driver calls this function
without HTTP. A LAPSED invoice may be reactivated only when no newer
revision exists in its chain (spec §4's single terminal exception,
taken through the transition helper's ``allow_reactivation`` hatch);
otherwise :class:`NewerRevisionExistsError` is raised. Any other
non-READY status refuses with :class:`ClaimRefusedError`. Never
commits; the caller owns the transaction.
signature: (session: Session, clock: Clock, auditor: User, invoice_id: int) -> Invoice

docstring:
Claim the top eligible invoice for ``auditor`` (spec Act 4).

Sets ``claimed_by`` and transitions READY → CLAIMED with the
auditor's short name as actor. An empty queue returns ``None`` —
not an error. Never commits; the caller owns the transaction.
signature: (session: Session, clock: Clock, auditor: User) -> Invoice | None

docstring:
Eligible invoices in queue order for one auditor.

Weight descending with the prior-auditor boost applied in memory —
the stored weight is never modified — and invoice id ascending as
the tiebreak.
signature: (session: Session, clock: Clock, config: InvoiceGuardConfig, auditor: User) -> list[Invoice]

docstring:
Roll-up: findings and benchmark signals become opportunity and weight.

The component ``ig.spine.rollup`` (spec §6, Act 3). Benchmark scoring
dispatches every invoice here; the calculation reduces the invoice's
findings plus its stored benchmark deltas to the two queue-driving
numbers and flips a freshly scored invoice from RECEIVED to READY.
Re-runs — late compliance reports, creep-back detections, feedback
recalculations, the nightly bulk pass — recompute in place using the
*stored* delta columns; benchmark HTTP is called exactly once per
invoice, by the benchmark-scoring stage, never from here.

The compliance-wait dance (spec Act 2): an invoice reaching roll-up
without a compliance report defers finalization behind a
``skip_compliance`` task. Exactly-once finalization hangs on the
invoice's own status — the RECEIVED → READY transition happens inside
:func:`calculate_rollup`, compliance intake finalizes only invoices
still RECEIVED behind an armed task, and the task handler no-ops for
anything no longer RECEIVED — so both arrival orders leave exactly one
transition in the history.
Whether any finding of a category still counts against the supplier.

Reduce one invoice's findings to opportunity and weight (spec §6).

Mirrors the spec's pseudocode order exactly:

1. Sum ``effective_amount()`` by MATERIAL / SERVICE / FEE (the
   excluded categories act later; an excepted finding contributes
   zero).
2. Benchmark branch — only when a stored ``service_hours_delta``
   exists: dollarize it at ``contract_labor_rate`` and count it only
   when positive and larger than the service sum it would replace.
3. Add the rules opportunity, weight both by their factors.
4. Multiply weight for creep-back and ignored-correction findings.
   Presence means at least one such finding *without* a
   valid-exception — those categories never reach the sums, so the
   multiplier is their only weight effect, and the spec's Act 3/4
   promise that excepting a finding removes its influence on the
   next recalc must hold here too.
5. A compliance-finding total at ``COMPLIANCE_SCORE_CRITICAL`` or
   above adds the flat weight — before the multiplier applies, per
   the pseudocode.
6. Normalize weight by invoice size (``invoice_total or 1`` guards
   both NULL and zero) plus the base-effort factor.

``alt_source_pct_delta`` is stored on the invoice but deliberately
excluded from every total: the alternate-sourcing benchmark is
pending validation (spec §6), so it surfaces as a signal without
moving money.

Completion stamps ``scored_at`` and flips RECEIVED to READY; any
other status is a recomputation in place, with no transition.
signature: (session: Session, clock: Clock, invoice: Invoice) -> None

docstring:
The convergence point every findings branch funnels into.

With a compliance report already in hand the invoice is scored and
finalized now. Without one, finalization is deferred: a
``skip_compliance`` task 60 minutes out (deduped per invoice)
guarantees scoring completes even if the report never comes, and an
arriving report triggers it sooner.
signature: (session: Session, clock: Clock, invoice: Invoice) -> None

docstring:
An uncompleted skip_compliance task already armed for this invoice.

Shared with compliance intake: an armed task is the proof that the
pipeline already deferred this invoice, which is what licenses the
intake side to finalize it early.

In-place recompute for invoices already past finalization.

The entry point for late findings producers (creep-back, late
compliance reports): READY, CLAIMED, or IN_REVIEW invoices get their
numbers refreshed with no status change; anything else — still
RECEIVED (findings will fold in at finalization) or terminal (never
re-scored) — is a logged no-op.
signature: (session: Session, clock: Clock, invoice: Invoice) -> None

docstring:
Scheduled-task handler for ``nightly_recalc`` (spec §7).

Bulk :func:`calculate_rollup` over the READY/RECEIVED backlog in
invoice-id order, so weights track the newest config and feedback.
Two kinds of RECEIVED invoice are skipped, and the distinction
matters — do not "simplify" it away:

- one named by an uncompleted ``hold_recheck`` task is mid-hold:
  its lines are mapped but its rules never ran, and recalculating
  would score it from NOTE findings alone and flip it queue-visible
  prematurely;
- one named by an uncompleted ``skip_compliance`` task is inside
  its compliance wait window, which this pass must not shorten.

RECEIVED invoices with no blocking task stay in scope deliberately:
a failed ``skip_compliance`` task is marked completed by the
executor, and this pass is what rescues the invoice it stranded.
signature: (session: Session, clock: Clock, args: dict) -> None

docstring:
Scheduled-task handler for ``skip_compliance`` (spec §7).

Finalizes an invoice still RECEIVED after the compliance wait —
roll-up without compliance findings. Any other status means the
report arrived first (already finalized) or the invoice left the
pipeline (lapsed/terminal): a logged no-op, which is the task-side
half of the exactly-once guarantee.
signature: (session: Session, clock: Clock, args: dict) -> None

docstring:
The rules engine: twelve audit rules over every mapped invoice.

The component ``ig.spine.rules-engine`` (spec §5, Act 2). Line mapping
dispatches here once per mapped invoice; each rule is its own function
with a named-constant tripping condition, and every finding goes through
the idempotent ``persist_finding`` seam. Tunable thresholds come from
the versioned config table; fixed thresholds are the module constants
below. When the walk finishes, the engine dispatches onward to
prior-audit compliance.

Finding categories follow the table in ``RULE_CATEGORIES``: line-scoped
dollar rules inherit their line's class (MATERIAL/SERVICE/FEE) so the
roll-up sums attribute dollars to the right bucket; the two amount-zero
informational flags are NOTE findings, which the roll-up excludes.

value: {'rate_variance': LINE_CLASS, 'unapproved_item': LINE_CLASS, 'quantity_spike': LINE_CLASS, 'duplicate_line': LINE_CLASS, 'new_supplier': FindingCategory.NOTE, 'freight_overcharge': FindingCategory.FEE, 'rush_fee_unjustified': FindingCategory.FEE, 'markup_over_list': LINE_CLASS, 'service_hours_excessive': FindingCategory.SERVICE, 'contract_lapsed_rate': LINE_CLASS, 'total_mismatch': FindingCategory.FEE, 'split_billing': FindingCategory.NOTE}

docstring:
The contract row covering an item at an instant.

Coverage: effective_from (unset means always) has passed and
effective_to (unset means open-ended) has not. Ties resolve to the
newest effective_from, then the highest row id, so the pick is
deterministic when windows overlap.
signature: (contracts: list[Contract], item_code: str, at: datetime) -> Contract | None

docstring: A line's own MATERIAL/SERVICE/FEE class as a finding category.
All of one supplier's contract rows, in a stable order.

A line still priced by an expired contract revision.

Trips when the unit rate exactly matches an expired contract row's
rate while the active contract prices the item lower — the supplier
kept billing the old, higher rate. Exact float equality is safe
here: matching rates come from the same decimal strings. The amount
is the delta back to the active rate.
signature: (session: Session, clock: Clock, invoice: Invoice, line: InvoiceLine, contracts: list[Contract]) -> None

docstring:
The same item, quantity, and rate billed twice.

Trips on a twin within the invoice, or in another of the supplier's
invoices received in the ``DUPLICATE_WINDOW_DAYS`` before this one.
The invoice's own revision chain is excluded — a revision repeating
its prior's lines is the normal case, not double billing. Detection
is one-directional (this invoice against what came before), so of a
cross-invoice pair only the later invoice trips.
signature: (session: Session, clock: Clock, invoice: Invoice, line: InvoiceLine, lines: list[InvoiceLine]) -> None

docstring:
Fee lines out of proportion to the goods they ride on.

Trips when the invoice's FEE total exceeds ``FREIGHT_PCT_CAP`` of
its MATERIAL subtotal; one invoice-level FEE finding carries the
excess. With no material on the invoice every fee dollar is excess.
signature: (session: Session, clock: Clock, invoice: Invoice, lines: list[InvoiceLine]) -> None

docstring:
A rate above the allowed markup over the item's list price.

Trips when the unit rate exceeds list price times
``list_markup_cap`` (config-tunable); the amount is the excess over
that allowance. Contracts without a list price cannot be judged.
signature: (session: Session, clock: Clock, invoice: Invoice, line: InvoiceLine, contracts: list[Contract], config) -> None

docstring:
A supplier still inside its first contract year gets a review flag.

Flat informational finding (amount 0) when the supplier was first
contracted within ``NEW_SUPPLIER_DAYS`` of this invoice. Suppliers
without a recorded first-contract date have no measurable age and do
not trip.
signature: (session: Session, clock: Clock, invoice: Invoice) -> None

docstring:
A quantity far above this supplier's history for the item.

Trips when the quantity exceeds ``QUANTITY_SPIKE_FACTOR`` times the
supplier's trailing average for the item — the mean line quantity
across the supplier's *other* invoices (the invoice's own revision
chain is excluded) received before this one. No history means no
baseline and no trip. The excess is measured against the average
itself: everything above normal usage is opportunity, not just the
part beyond the trip threshold.
signature: (session: Session, clock: Clock, invoice: Invoice, line: InvoiceLine) -> None

docstring:
A line billed meaningfully above its contracted rate.

Trips when the unit rate exceeds the active contract rate by more
than ``rate_variance_pct`` (config-tunable). The recovery amount is
the full delta back to contract, not just the part beyond the
threshold.
signature: (session: Session, clock: Clock, invoice: Invoice, line: InvoiceLine, contracts: list[Contract], config) -> None

docstring:
A rush fee on an invoice that was never flagged rush.

A rush-fee line is a FEE line whose description mentions
``RUSH_FEE_KEYWORD``; when the invoice's rush flag is false the
whole fee is recovery.
signature: (session: Session, clock: Clock, invoice: Invoice, line: InvoiceLine) -> None

docstring:
A service line burning more hours per unit than its class allows.

The cap is the config-tunable per-item-class mapping (the item class
is the item code's prefix before the first dash; the required
``"default"`` key covers unlisted classes). Excess hours are
dollarized at the line's own implied hourly rate — extended price
over service hours — not the per-unit rate.
signature: (session: Session, clock: Clock, invoice: Invoice, line: InvoiceLine, config) -> None

docstring:
Several same-day invoices quietly splitting one PO past approval.

Trips when this invoice shares its PO reference with at least one
other invoice number from the supplier on the same received day and
the group's totals jointly exceed ``po_approval_threshold``
(config-tunable). Revision chains count once, at their newest
revision. Flat flag, amount 0.
signature: (session: Session, clock: Clock, invoice: Invoice, config) -> None

docstring:
A stated total that disagrees with the lines, unexplained.

Trips when the invoice total differs from the sum of extended
prices by more than ``TOTAL_MISMATCH_TOLERANCE`` and the adjustment
flag is false. A true adjustment flag makes the mismatch legitimate
(spec §9's planted gotcha) — deliberately no finding.
signature: (session: Session, clock: Clock, invoice: Invoice, lines: list[InvoiceLine]) -> None

docstring:
A line for an item the supplier has no active contract for.

Everything billed off-contract is recovery opportunity, so the
amount is the full extended price.
signature: (session: Session, clock: Clock, invoice: Invoice, line: InvoiceLine, contracts: list[Contract]) -> None

docstring:
Apply every audit rule to one mapped invoice, then dispatch on.

Walks lines in line-number order, then the invoice-level rules, so
findings and logs are order-stable across identical runs. Re-runs
add nothing: every write goes through ``persist_finding``.
signature: (session: Session, clock: Clock, invoice: Invoice) -> None
